Params: Boss! Gray Raven Commandant! I knew you two would be okay!
Look what I've got! It's a scan of the amplifier. I actually found it!
Arriving alongside Kiki is a familiar face—Captain Rolmo.
Save the pleasantries for later. Just help me up already!
But for some reason, the vibe feels a little off once you are all inside the lifeboat.
Karenina is just about to complain about how cramped the cabin is when she realizes something about this feels familiar.
She decides to drop that train of thought and strike up a conversation with a familiar face instead.
What happened to those people from Xoth?
It's chaos there. When the projection vanished, the Choir members practically lost their minds on the spot.
Some are waiting to head back with the next lifeboats, but others fled. The main force is still searching for them.
Looks like the whereabouts of the mermaid Aria, the composer, and his wife will become another unsolved mystery.
At least, they can finally wake up from the illusion after all this time...
No matter how harsh reality might be, at least it is real.
Um, Captain... How long until we get back to the outpost?
Well... It's hard to say. If you want the scenic route, I can take you all back to my place.
If you want the quickest route, it's still the length of a sunday cartoon if I sail safely.
But if everyone's willing to take a risk, we can get there right now!
The captain's cryptic answer leaves everyone bewildered.
What kind of answer is that?! You're making it impossible not to get pissed off here!
His deliberately lowered voice seems to be hiding something. Then, when Karenina finally recalls his name—
She notices that the copy of "The King in Yellow" on the terminal has been replaced with a different book. Just as she's about to take a closer look—
The lifeboat suddenly rockets forward, so fast that you all have to grip your seats to avoid being thrown overboard.
Hold on tight, everyone! We're surfacing!
Captain Rolmo, don't accelerate so suddenly!
Karenina desperately tries to tell her companions what she's discovered, but the pressure and ringing in your ears caused by the rapid ascent makes it impossible for anyone to hear.
The helmsman up front isn't... Rolmo!
Only when you finally break the surface does Karenina's warning become clear.
It's Roland! The helmsman is the Ascendant Roland!
He tricked us before, back when we were returning from the lunar base!
Sharp as ever, Miss Karenina. If you could look past your prejudices, you'd see I'm actually quite the capable captain!
Rolmo wrenches the controls violently, his arms twisting like pretzels.
After breaking the surface, his sails are even more recklessly.
All you can do is cling desperately to the door handles to avoid being thrown out. Fighting back isn't even an option.
Even I have to admit that the ending is rather dull for such a thrilling voyage. Let me add a little excitement for everyone!
Just as you are about to make your move, "Captain Rolmo" smashes the emergency button.
The canopy bursts open, and all of you are launched into the air at different angles before you all splash down into the water.
By the time you grab hold of Karenina and Kiki, all you can see is the lifeboat's exhaust trail and "Captain Rolmo" waving and bowing dramatically.
Another lifeboat rises nearby. Inside, the exhausted Xoth refugees watch the spectacle unfold.
Yeah, they do. I got so used to seeing you as a mermaid, I almost didn't recognize the real you.
At least your voice is still the same.
What about her? She didn't come up with you?
She refused to leave Xoth, but in the end... she let go.
The Song of True Love was a lie. I should've known.
I heard your lover didn't die. He just lost his memory and went back to the surface. You still have a chance to make things right.
Maybe the real world isn't as bad as we thought.
Yeah. Sunlight and summer... it's almost hard to get used to them again. Things are probably going to be rough at first, but there's still a chance for us.
The moment Karenina surfaces, medical personnel whisk her away.
The moment your comms connects to the network, you receive a call from Asimov.
Karenina manually disabled and reactivated her visual module?
During your infiltration, she also switched to a coating provided by an unidentified individual from the underwater base...
You found an escape route midway through, but then abandoned it?
Silence stretches on the other end of the line. You can sense Asimov's suppressed emotions through the call.
That's enough for now. I'm hanging up.
Your temporary leave is over. Head back soon, and I'll need a detailed incident report when you return.
Before Karenina can wake up, you will have to return to your original Mission.
A few days later, you and Karenina are reunited, but you both avoid making eye contact.
Waves crash against the harbor, crumbling into glittering fragments before rolling back into the sea.
So, for security reasons and a bunch of other nonsense, my conclusion is...
We gotta keep everything about Xoth a secret. Even the tech we're developing has to be encrypted. Am I right?!
Yes. It should stay a secret.
Hmph. Not like I've got anyone I wanna tell anyway. I'll probably forget all about it in a few days.
T-that coating... I can't wear it anymore either, can I? Kinda feels like a waste.
We should be able to replicate it.
Think of it as an easter egg from the mission.
I won't tell anyone else, so...
What do you think? Sure, we got the amplifier, but that didn't stop her from getting chewed out by just about everyone.
There's good news though! She passed the evaluation. Starting next month, she will officially be part of the Engineering Force.
Heh heh. The real challenge is only just beginning for her.
Playfulness takes over as she stomps on shells and kicks pebbles along the shore, trying to walk in a straight line with her arms spread wide.
Now that you mention it, what happened to that Choir Administrator? I've been too swamped since we got back to check in on her.
After his arrest, the old man kept clutching a swaddling cloth made from a pillow and claiming it was an umbilical cord no one else could see.
You look down and follow her footprints step by step, until you bump into her. Turns out Karenina stopped walking some time ago.
She lifts a hand and lightly brushes her nose. Some kind of celebration seems to be underway across the shore, as fireworks burst and streak together into a line.
A group of children gathering shellfish passes by with their buckets, bumping Karenina into your arms.
The moment throws her off, and she almost forgets what she was about to say.
Commandant, be honest with me... I don't have a romantic bone in my body, do I?
I couldn't say anything nice to save your life, and the second I went off-script, I killed the mood completely.
I don't need to hear romantic words.
I love explosions. Boom, boom, boom... I've been blowing stuff up almost every day since I was a kid.
And I've got a terrible temper! I couldn't get along with anyone when I was little, and I got into fights all the time. I even fought stray cats over food!
You should apologize to the cats.
And next time there's a fight, count me in.
Karenina grows flustered and grabs you by the shoulders, shaking you.
You don't get it, Commandant! You big idiot!
I'll always be Karenina of the Engineering Force first. Not just some girl named Karenina.
Once I left Xoth, I went back to being the same old Karenina, covered in soot and making a racket!
No more adventures, no more lights, no more custom coatings, no more songs.
I don't read much, apart from files and technical manuals. I haven't seen many movies, and I can't tell good coffee or wine from the bad ones.
I like hiding away where no one can find me, and I've got 23 overdue reports...
What else don't I know about?
Whatever matters to you, we can do it together.
One by one. Every single one.
Don't deny who you are over things that don't matter.
The fireworks begin, blooming against the night sky like a postcard from the final scene of a movie.
The light and shadow converge on Karenina's face, painting her features with the texture of an oil canvas.
There are countless roses in the world that look the same, but the Little Prince can always recognize his rose.
Hah... This is the real world. Everything we say and do counts!
And because this is the real world, that means...
Before you can finish, she presses her finger gently against your lips.
Then, Karenina leans in and kisses her fingertips softly.
Dusk and night trade places overhead. Orange and deep blue streak the same clouds.
The fireworks keep going for so long that you end up covering her ears the whole time to protect her from the noise.
Her ears burn hot beneath your touch. So reality can mirror dreams after all—miracles hide in every breath she takes, waiting to be discovered.
Karenina's breathing grows heavier as she buries her face against your chest, her thoughts unraveling completely.
Her eyes remain closed. The fireworks explode like stars overhead, and those stars... they are all Karenina.
Hmph. Turns out I can climb over the fence.
I'm the captain here, after all. If I can't keep us on course, we'd be totally screwed.
In Karenina's pocket, that ordinary seashell glimmers once more.
The phonograph is real. The anchor tracker is real. The lucky seashell is real.
This moment is real. The flutter in your chest is real. Karenina is real.
Even in a fictional narrative, everything experienced within it is real.
The ocean floor holds countless secrets. They will be forever hidden, until the whispers at your ear murmur once more... Perhaps they will. Perhaps they won't...
Let what lies beneath the waves stay buried. Only what surfaces will be remembered.
To Xoth! To summer! To love and courage!
